event: Iranian state media announce a temporary closure of the strait (or parts of it) for live-fire drills; AP could not confirm it took effect.
Windward counts 120 crossings (pre-war reference day).
Flightradar24 counts 1,257 flights at Dubai, the last normal day.
Trump reportedly gives the order to proceed with Operation Epic Fury.

time_note: between about 05:57 and 06:30 UTC; sources conflict
event: First explosions reported in Tehran and other cities; Israel announces a 'preemptive strike', a US official confirms a joint operation.
CENTCOM announces that strikes have begun.

time_note: about; Wikipedia only for the time
event: A strike on the leadership compound kills Ali Khamenei and other senior officials (confirmed by Iranian state TV about 01:30 UTC on 1 Mar).

time_note: about; Euronews live-blog log time, lags the event
event: Israel closes its airspace to civilian flights; Iran announces a nationwide closure.
A missile hits a girls' school beside an IRGC base; death toll reported between 153 and 182. A preliminary US inquiry reportedly pointed to a US targeting error.
Trump announces 'major combat operations in Iran'.

time_note: about; statement logged by Euronews; Wikipedia says launches from 09:05
event: Iran retaliates with missiles and drones; the IRGC names Al Udeid, Ali Al Salem, Al Dhafra and Fifth Fleet HQ.
Iraq closes its airspace.
A missile strikes the US Fifth Fleet service centre.
UAE airspace closes (WAM: 'temporarily and partially'; ch-aviation: closed to all commercial traffic). At least eight states close fully or partly on the day.
Dubai Airports suspends all flights; Emirates, flydubai, Qatar Airways and Kuwait Airways suspend operations.
EASA issues conflict-zone bulletin CZIB 2026-03 covering 11 flight information regions.
Ships receive IRGC VHF radio messages that no ship may pass; Iran makes no formal closure declaration. At least three tankers halt outbound voyages.
Kpler: at least five very large crude carriers turn away from the strait.
Windward: about 1,100 vessels affected by GPS/AIS interference in the first 24 hours.

place: Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman
event: MarineTraffic data (Reuters): at least 150 tankers anchored in open Gulf waters, at least 100 more off the UAE and Oman.
First tankers hit: Skylight, MKD Vyom, Hercules Star; Ocean Electra reports a near miss.
P&I clubs issue war-risk cancellation notices (72 hours' notice; effective date reported as 2 Mar by Windward and 5 Mar by Al Jazeera).
IRGC adviser Ebrahim Jabari: 'The strait is closed'; ships trying to pass will be set 'ablaze'. CENTCOM reportedly says the strait is still open.
QatarEnergy halts LNG production after drone attacks; Iran denies targeting it.
First Emirates flight (EK500) leaves Dubai. Flightradar24 counts 20 flights at Dubai for the day.
S&P: seven ships transit, against nine on 2 Mar and a February average of 91. Windward: four crossings.
Trump orders US political-risk insurance and says the Navy will escort tankers 'if necessary'; the Joint War Committee widens its high-risk area.
The UAE opens 'safe corridors' at 48 flights per hour.
The IRGC claims full control of the strait.
Ben Gurion reopens to prior-approved flights.
P&I war-risk cancellations take effect (Al Jazeera's date).
The IRGC says the strait is closed only to US, Israeli and allied ships.
Flightradar24: Dubai 310 flights; Muscat 280, double the 140 of 1 Mar.
Qatar partially reopens airspace for evacuation and cargo flights only.
The US announces up to $20bn in maritime reinsurance.
Windward: more than 1,650 vessels with interference, up 55% in a week; cluster shapes change from circles to zig-zags.

time_note: FIRMS detection time attributed to Al Jazeera, not confirmed
event: Israel strikes Tehran-area fuel depots, its first strikes on Iranian oil facilities (date reported as 6, 7 or 8 Mar).
Windward: two crossings, both Iranian-flagged.
Mojtaba Khamenei is named supreme leader (some sources say 9 Mar). Brent passes $100.
Trump says the strait is 'open'.
Planet extends its imagery delay from 4 to 14 days over Iran, the Gulf and allied bases; Vantor applies access controls. Free public satellites are unaffected.
A radar satellite pass finds eight large vessels with no AIS broadcast; Windward counts two crossings for the day.
JMIC: more than 600 GNSS disruption events in 24 hours; spoofing first seen off Ras Al Khaimah.
The Energy Secretary posts, then retracts, a claim that the Navy escorted a tanker. CENTCOM says it sank 16 Iranian minelayers.

place: 11 nm north of Oman, in the strait
event: Bulk carrier Mayuree Naree is hit and set on fire; ONE Majesty and Star Gwyneth damaged. UKMTO has logged 17 incidents since 28 Feb.
UN Security Council Resolution 2817 condemns Iran's attacks in the Gulf, 13-0-2.
Mojtaba Khamenei's first statement vows to keep Hormuz closed. The US Energy Secretary says the Navy is not ready to escort tankers.
The US bombs more than 90 military targets on Kharg Island; oil infrastructure is spared, per both US and Iranian officials.
Windward: zero AIS-confirmed transits, the first such day.
Araghchi says the strait is open except to US and Israeli vessels. About 400 ships wait in the Gulf of Oman.
